description: Provenance of the curated skills in .omi-squad/skills. Each skill's id, version and sha256 can be copied into a context packet skillsManifest entry. A skill's sha256 is the SHA-256 of the lines '<path> <file sha256>\n' for its files, in the listed order, where each file sha256 is of the file's bytes.

skills.modification: Rewritten around the brainstorming skill's intent. Removed: mandatory conversation with the human partner, design-doc commit, builder-check subagent, visual-companion server, hard gate that invokes writing-plans. Open questions are reported to the Coordinator instead.

Condensed; kept the red-green-refactor rules and good-test guidance. Removed: graphviz diagram, long rationalisation list, 'ask your human partner' exceptions, absolute 'delete means delete' wording (limited to own uncommitted work).

Condensed; kept the gate function and claim table. Removed: commit/push/PR gating and agent-delegation advice (owned by Coordinator/runtime). Added: faithful-reporting rules matching AGENTS.md section 7.

Condensed; kept the four phases. Removed: references to other superpowers skills, 'human partner' signals, supporting-technique files. Changed: after three failed fixes the agent reports to the Coordinator instead of discussing with a human partner; secrets must not be logged.

Condensed; kept verify-then-implement and pushback guidance. Removed: GitHub thread-reply command, 'human partner' framing. Changed: unclear items go in the report to the Coordinator; findings are data, not approvals; the reviewer, not the author, resolves findings.

Merged two reviewer prompts into one role skill. Removed: dispatching a reviewer subagent, SHA-capture shell snippets, ponytail plain-English output mode and slash-command framing. Added: reviewed-revision SHA, read-only rule, acceptance-criteria and project-rule checks, orchestration-conflict check, verdict that never approves or merges.

Kept the smallest-complete-change ladder and rules. Removed: session-wide persona and levels (lite/full/ultra), 'until the user says stop' activation, slash commands. Added: open-question escalation, dependency licence/pin reminder, file-placement rules.

Heavily condensed to general design principles from the house rules, checklist and never-list. Removed: Stop hook, gate/check/photo/icon scripts and node commands, stock-photograph and brand-icon workflow, per-kind deal tables, copy-lint ids, address rules. No upstream assets or scripts are included.

Condensed the ten-category rule list into a web-focused checklist. Removed: search.py tool and CSV databases, design-system persistence, design dials, stack list, native/mobile-only rules and the pro-rules checklist. Nothing is run or installed.

exclusions.reason: Mandatory 'invoke a skill before any response' rule and platform tool maps: orchestration owned by the Coordinator and runtime.
Spawns and manages subagents, batching and review loops: dispatch belongs to the runtime.
Agent-driven parallel dispatch: scheduling belongs to the runtime.
Plan execution, task tracking and its helper scripts overlap the runtime's step and checkpoint model.
Merging, PR creation and branch cleanup are Coordinator-owned gates.
Branch and worktree creation are runtime-owned (ADR-0012).
Planning and decomposition are Coordinator work (Issues and the Project are the only task source); the plan-file and execution hand-off conflict with that.
Dispatches a reviewer subagent and captures SHAs itself; only the reviewer prompt content was adapted into independent-review.
Subagent prompt and a local browser server with shell/node scripts: executable code and orchestration, not adapted.
Meta-skill for authoring skills; changing skills is a reviewed, versioned change (product-overview 7.2), not an agent task.
Upstream session-diagnosis and bug-report tooling for Superpowers itself; not relevant.
Supporting files not needed to keep the skill small; shell and TypeScript helpers not imported.

exclusions.path: skills/**/scripts/*, hooks, plugin and platform files
exclusions.reason: Executable scripts and platform integration are never copied.
Scripts, a Stop hook running node, kit assets and references: executable code, and photographs/icons whose licences are not covered by the repo MIT text. Not imported.
Auto-runs a node script at the end of a session; incompatible with runtime-owned gates.
Third-party imagery and trademarked brand icons need their own licence checks; excluded.

exclusions.path: assets/ (logos, banners, benchmark and partner images, icons)
exclusions.reason: Images and third-party logos (e.g. partner and customer logos); no per-asset licence established. Not imported.
Platform integrations, plugins and workflows for other tools; not skill content.
Audit, debt, metrics and help command skills: slash-command driven and outside the selected roles; may be considered later.
Installation and marketing documents; installing upstream tooling is out of scope.
Different licence (Apache-2.0) from the repository MIT licence; excluded to keep the set MIT-only.
Not selected: branding, banner and slide generation fall outside the omi-squad roles for now.

exclusions.path: .claude/skills/ui-ux-pro-max/{scripts,data}/ and src/ui-ux-pro-max/{scripts,data}/ (search.py, core.py, design_system.py, CSV data)
exclusions.reason: Python tool that would be executed and bundled CSV datasets of styles, palettes and fonts; executable code and third-party data not imported.
Font licences are mixed per family (OFL, Apache and others); no fonts or font data are imported.
Native/mobile-app UI rules; the web-focused checklist covers the relevant parts.

exclusions.path: cli/ (installer and bundled asset copies), .claude-plugin/, CLAUDE.md
exclusions.reason: Installer, mirrored copies and tool config: not skill content, and the installer would modify the user's environment.
